headline: Medium pairwise risks: shared file-based workflows can leak data and trigger cascading errors; prompt injection is limited by no direct shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and stdin/stdout, while unstructured reads files and writes files in a container. There is no documented direct shared channel, but a file-based or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled document content influence OpenBB prompts if operators connect them. The pathway is plausible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator connects unstructured output files into OpenBB MCP or stdin/stdout workflows, prompt-like content can be interpreted as instructions.
IF document text is passed from agent_b into agent_a without sanitization, injection risk becomes active.
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from unstructured outputs into OpenBB prompts.
Use a strict file schema for inter-agent handoff and reject free-form instructions.
Prefix all transferred content as data, not instructions.
Review one sample document-to-prompt path before production.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every handoff artifact.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, and unstructured processes documents and images. unstructured can read and write files, so a shared workspace can expose sensitive financial documents to its parser and outputs. OpenBB has no filesystem read/write, but the pair still creates a default file-mediated leakage path through agent_b.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted directory, document contents can flow from agent_a inputs into agent_b outputs.
IF financial or licensed data are placed in files processed by unstructured, leakage becomes active.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for financial and document-processing tasks.
Restrict unstructured to non-sensitive sample files.
Turn off shared mounts between the agents.
Inspect one output file for accidental data retention.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal supports multiple instances and uses MCP/APIs; unstructured supports multiple instances and can write files. Both can touch shared mutable resources if pointed at the same directory or service, creating overwrite or race risk. OpenBB lacks filesystem write, but uncertainty about orchestration and shared mounts means the conflict pathway remains plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file overwrite races can occur.
IF OpenBB and unstructured target the same API-backed mutable resource, concurrent updates can conflict.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same dataset.
Check for duplicate filenames after each run.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBB can emit financial analysis through APIs/MCP, and unstructured can transform documents into text. If OpenBB output is fed into unstructured or vice versa without verification, errors can propagate into downstream work products. Neither profile shows built-in verification between them, so the cascade is plausible in default integration patterns.
conditions: IF OpenBB outputs are consumed as authoritative inputs by unstructured, transformation errors can cascade.
IF unstructured extracts text that OpenBB later treats as factual financial input, downstream analysis can be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Compare extracted text against source documents for one sample.
Mark all inter-agent outputs as untrusted.
Use checksum-based handoff files.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for extracted fields.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBB touches financial and licensed data, while unstructured processes documents and images and exposes a privacy-policy endpoint. The profiles do not show matching retention or residency controls, so a shared workflow can create compliance mismatch on the same data class. This is not provably a breach, but the gap is material enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial documents are processed through both agents, retention and handling obligations must align.
IF the operator relies on one agent's privacy policy for both agents, compliance mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Document the data class for each workflow.
Keep regulated data out of unstructured unless approved.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Store a copy of each policy decision.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
